diagnostics.help: Pull each section into its own component so the parent is easier to read, test, and change.

diagnostics.title: Intl formatter rebuilt each call
diagnostics.message: This is slow because new Intl.DateTimeFormat() rebuilds on every call inside a function, so move it to the top of the file, or wrap it in useMemo
diagnostics.help: Move `new Intl.NumberFormat(...)` to the top of the file or wrap it in `useMemo`. Building one is slow, so don't redo it on every call

diagnostics.title: Heavy library loaded eagerly
diagnostics.message: "recharts" ships extra code to your users up front & slows page load. Load it on demand with React.lazy() or next/dynamic.
diagnostics.help: Load it only when needed: `const Component = dynamic(() => import('library'), { ssr: false })` from next/dynamic, or React.lazy().

diagnostics.title: State adjusted after a prop changes
diagnostics.message: This effect adjusts state after a prop changes, so users briefly see the stale value.
diagnostics.help: Remove the adjustment effect by deriving values during render, resetting the component with a key, or updating related state in the event that changes the prop. Avoid tracking the previous prop in more state, which preserves the duplication. See https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#adjusting-some-state-when-a-prop-changes

diagnostics.title: useMemo before an early return
diagnostics.message: This rebuilds the JSX whenever its dependencies change even on renders that take the early return, so move the JSX into a child component rendered after the early return to skip it
diagnostics.help: Move the JSX into a child component rendered after the early return, so renders that take the early return never build it

diagnostics.title: JSON parse/stringify deep clone
diagnostics.message: `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))` deep-clones by re-serializing: it is slow on large objects and silently drops `undefined`, functions, `Date`/`Map`/`Set`, and cyclic references. Use `structuredClone(x)`.
diagnostics.help: Replace `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value))` with `structuredClone(value)`. It is faster and preserves Dates, Maps, Sets, and cyclic references.
